I've saved the Q3 answers to `answer.json`. To check the method, I ran the same code on Q2 first, and it reproduced all ten of your reference values exactly.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Top segment by net sales | consumer, 352,803,010 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 249 |
| c. Top category by net sales | hw, 290,199,453 |
| d. Month with highest net sales | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with largest total refunds | u33@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 239 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 699,342 |
| h. Sept vs. Aug growth | −3.9% |

The definitions alone didn't reproduce the Q2 values. Three extra rules were needed, and I chose them because they make Q2 match:

1. **Korean time for dates:** I converted `ordered_at` from UTC to Korean time (+9 hours) before assigning orders to a quarter or month. Some orders sit right at the boundary (for example, 2025-09-30 14:30 UTC), so they move to the next day.
2. **One customer per email:** several customer IDs share the same email, so I counted customers by email (trimmed, lowercased) for b and f.
3. **Normalized segment and category names:** some segment values have stray spaces or different capitalization ("Enterprise ", " consumer", "SMB"/"smb"), so I trimmed and lowercased them before grouping. I did the same for category names.

STATUS: DONE
